prompt: Price a small Shipment hierarchy (Letter, Parcel, Pallet) with Java 17 pattern matching for instanceof: costCents, labelFor and a totalCents that skips nulls.
explanation: Pattern matching for instanceof tests the runtime type and binds a correctly typed variable in one step, so there is no separate cast to get wrong. The order of the tests does not matter here because the three record types are unrelated siblings, but the final fall-through return is what makes null and any unknown Shipment safe. Integer arithmetic keeps the fragile surcharge exact: multiplying by 125 and dividing by 100 avoids floating-point cents entirely.
hints: Test each record type with instanceof and give the test a binding variable; inside the block that variable already has the narrowed type, so you can call its accessors directly.
Compute the parcel base price first and only then apply the fragile surcharge with cost * 125 / 100.
A pallet charges for kilos ABOVE 10, so the extra is kilos - 10 but never less than zero.
